items.q: What does the law of superposition say about undisturbed rock layers?
options: Lower layers are younger than the layers above
Lower layers are older than the layers above them
All layers are the same age
items.why: Each layer is laid down on top of older ones, so in undisturbed layers the lower layers are older.

items.q: In a cliff of flat layers, where is the youngest layer?
items.why: The top layer was laid down last, so it is the youngest.

items.q: Layers W (top), X, Y and Z (bottom) have not been disturbed. Which is the oldest?
items.why: Z is at the bottom, so it formed first.

items.q: What is relative dating?
options: Putting rocks or events in order from oldest to youngest
Finding the exact age of a rock in years
Measuring how thick a layer is
Naming the minerals in a rock
items.why: Relative dating says which is older or younger, not how many years old.

items.q: A fossil trilobite is found two layers below a fossil fern in undisturbed rock. What can you say?
options: The fern lived before the trilobite
They lived at the same time
The trilobite lived before the fern
items.why: The trilobite's layer is lower, so it is older.

items.q: Why must the layers be undisturbed for the simple rule 'lower = older' to work?
options: Disturbed layers are made of granite
Earth movements can tilt, fold or flip layers
items.why: Folding can turn a stack upside down, putting the oldest layer on top.

items.q: Which type of rock forms in layers and is used most with the law of superposition?
items.why: Sediment settles in layers that harden into sedimentary rock.

items.q: A layer of sandstone is much thicker than the shale above it. Which is true?
options: The sandstone is older because it is thicker
The shale is older because it is thinner
Thickness shows they are the same age
The sandstone is older because it is lower
items.why: Position, not thickness, gives relative age.

items.q: Who first described the law of superposition, in 1669?
items.why: The Danish scientist Nicolas Steno described it in 1669.

items.q: Sediment settling on a sea floor is buried by more sediment. Which statement is right?
options: The buried sediment was there first
Both formed at exactly the same time
items.why: Whatever is underneath had to be there before the next layer could cover it.

items.q: Layers that were tilted after they formed are still in order. How do you read them?
options: The highest point of the cliff is always oldest
Follow the layers along the slope: each one lies on top of an older one
Tilted layers can't be dated at all
items.why: Tilting doesn't change which layer is on top of which.

items.q: What does relative dating NOT tell you?
options: How many years ago a layer formed
The order the layers formed in
items.why: For ages in years you need absolute (radiometric) dating.

items.q: In the Illawarra escarpment, the coal measures are at the bottom and the Hawkesbury Sandstone is at the top. Which formed first?
options: You can't tell from the cliff
items.why: The layers are almost flat, so the bottom (coal measures) formed first.

items.q: Why can each rock layer tell us about a different time in the past?
options: All layers formed in one big flood
Each layer was laid down at a different time, burying what lived then
Layers move around underground and mix
Rock layers are made by plants growing
items.why: Each layer records the time and place it was laid down, including fossils of life at that time.

items.q: A geologist logs a cliff from the bottom up. Why start at the bottom?
options: Because in undisturbed layers that is the order they formed in
Because the bottom is easiest to reach
Because the top layers have no rock
Because fossils are only at the bottom
items.why: Reading upward follows the order of deposition.

items.q: Which is a clue that a layer is upside down?
options: Pebbles and coarse grains are at the top of the layer instead of the bottom
items.why: Coarse grains settle first, so they mark the original bottom of a layer (graded bedding).

items.q: Layer B is above layer A and below layer C, and nothing has disturbed them. Put them oldest to youngest.
items.why: A is at the bottom, then B, then C on top.

items.q: Fossils of the same kind are found in a layer near the bottom of one cliff only. What does this suggest?
options: That organism is still alive today
That organism lived early in the time these rocks record
items.why: Lower layers are older, so the organism lived early in that record.

items.q: Volcanic ash falls on a lake and becomes a layer. Later, mud covers it. Which is older?
items.why: The ash was there first and was covered by mud later.

items.q: Which best describes 'strata'?
items.why: Strata (singular: stratum) are layers of rock.

items.q: A dyke cuts through layers 1 to 4 but not layer 5 on top. Which is true?
options: The dyke is older than all the layers
The dyke is younger than all the layers
The dyke is the same age as layer 1
The dyke is younger than layers 1 to 4 and older than layer 5
items.why: Cross-cutting relationships: a rock that cuts others is younger than them.

items.q: How do geologists find a layer's age in years?
options: Radiometric dating of minerals such as zircon in volcanic ash
Using the law of superposition alone
items.why: Radioactive atoms decay at known rates, giving absolute ages.

items.q: What does an erosion surface between two layers (an unconformity) mean?
options: The layers formed at the same time
Some time is missing from the rock record there
items.why: Rock was worn away before the next layer was laid down, so there is a time gap.

items.q: What is the principle of original horizontality?
options: All layers are tilted when they form
Sediment is laid down in roughly flat layers, so tilted layers were moved later
Only igneous rocks form flat layers
items.why: Steno also noticed that sediment settles flat; tilting comes afterwards.
